newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-TRADE TO UKRAINE DOUBLES SINCE MID-96-AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-TRADE TO UKRAINE DOUBLES SINCE MID-96-AGENCY.

text.p: Estonia's trade to the Ukraine has doubled in the past six months since the two countries agreed on a zero tariff agreement, Estonia's Investment Agency said on Thursday.
"Ukraine with over 50 million people is a big market and it will build up further," the agency's general director Juri Sakkeus told Reuters in an interview.
"There is talk of Ukraine increasing import tariffs so this will give Estonia a further advantage with the zero tariff arrangement set for an indefinite period."
The two countries agreed on a zero tariff arrangement in the second half of 1996.
In the first half of 1996 trade with Ukraine made up three percent of Estonia's trade.
Estonia's largest trade partners were Finland with a 29 percent slice, Russia with 14 percent, Sweden with 10 percent and Germany with nine percent.
"We are seeing Ukraine becoming more important with a lot of food products going there from Estonia," Sakkeus said.
The volume of exports in 1996 was estimated at 24 billion kroons and this was forecast to rise to 28 billion kroons in 1997.
The volume of imports to Estonia was 35 billion kroons in 1995 and expected to rise to 38.4 billion kroons in 1997.

"But the growth of the volume of imports is expected to slow down in the coming years and thus the trade balance deficit is expected to stabilise and finally to decrease by the turn of the century," the agency said.
